content: Hydrocortisone, neomycin, and polymyxin are prescribed to treat bacterial infections of the ear, eye, and skin. This combination medication works by eliminating the bacteria causing the infection and alleviating associated symptoms such as pain, inflammation, redness, and itching. It may also be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. This medication is available in the form of ear drops, eye drops, and a skin cream. For eye infections, it is typically used every 3 to 4 hours. For ear and skin infections, it is usually applied 2 to 4 times a day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the medication exactly as directed. Do not use more or less of it, or use it more frequently than prescribed. Do not use this medication for more than 10 days. If your infection does not improve within one week or worsens, contact your doctor. Instructions for Ear Drops: 1. Gently clean and dry your ear with a sterile cotton swab. 2. Wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water. 3. Inspect the dropper to ensure it is not chipped or cracked. 4. Keep the dropper clean and avoid touching it to your ear, fingers, or any other surface to prevent contamination. 5. Warm the drops to near body temperature by holding the container in your hand for a few minutes. 6. If the drops are a cloudy suspension, shake the container well for 10 seconds. 7. Draw the prescribed amount of medication into the dropper. 8. Tilt your head so the affected ear is facing upward, or lie on your side with the affected ear up. 9. For adults, pull the earlobe up and back; for children, pull the earlobe down and back to allow the drops to flow in. 10. Place the prescribed number of drops into the ear and keep your head tilted for 5 minutes. Do not insert the dropper into your ear to avoid injury. 11. If preferred, you may use a soft cotton gauze wick plug saturated with the ear drops. Keep the cotton moist by adding drops every 4 hours or as directed by your doctor, and replace the cotton every 24 hours. 12. Wash your hands after application to remove any medication. Instructions for Eye Drops: 1. Shake the bottle well before use. 2. Wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water. 3. Use a mirror or have someone else help you apply the drops. 4. Ensure the dropper tip is not chipped or cracked. 5. Avoid touching the dropper to your eye or any surface to prevent contamination. Always keep the dropper tip facing downward to prevent backflow into the bottle. 6. Lie down or tilt your head back. 7. Hold the bottle between your thumb and index finger, positioning the dropper tip close to your eyelid without touching it. 8. Brace the remaining fingers of that hand against your cheek or nose. 9. With the index finger of your other hand, pull the lower eyelid down to form a pocket. 10. Drop the prescribed number of drops into the pocket formed by the lower eyelid. Avoid placing drops directly on the eyeball, as this may cause stinging. 11. Close your eye for 2 to 3 minutes to allow the medication to be absorbed. Do not blink. 12. Replace and tighten the cap immediately after use. Do not wipe or rinse the dropper. 13. Wipe off any excess liquid from your cheek with a clean tissue. 14. Wash your hands again to remove any medication. Instructions for Skin Cream: 1. Wash the affected skin area thoroughly. 2. Apply a small amount of cream and rub it in gently. 3. If using the cream on your face, avoid contact with your eyes. 4. Do not bandage or wrap the treated area unless directed by your doctor. 5. Do not apply the cream to other areas of the body unless instructed by your doctor. 6. Avoid using cosmetics or other skin preparations on the treated area without consulting your doctor. 7. If applying the cream to a child’s diaper area, avoid tight-fitting diapers or plastic pants, as this may increase side effects. Special Precautions: Inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to hydrocortisone, neomycin, polymyxin, or any other drugs. Provide your doctor with a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially cancer chemotherapy agents, other topical medications, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had kidney disease, a heart attack, diabetes, glaucoma, cataracts, a perforated eardrum, a circulation disorder, or an immune disorder. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using this medication, contact your doctor immediately. What to Do If You Miss a Dose: Apply the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one. Side Effects: Minor Side Effects: This medication may cause the following side effects. Contact your doctor if these symptoms are severe or persistent: Itching Burning Pain Swelling Drying or cracking of the skin Acne Changes in skin color Blurred vision Hearing difficulty Severe Side Effects: If you experience any of the following symptoms, contact your doctor immediately: Severe skin rash Difficulty breathing or swallowing Wheezing If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Storage Instructions: Keep this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Store it according to the package instructions. Dispose of any outdated or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. Additional Information: Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share this medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
